SOURCE: "FacTool: Factuality Detection in Generative AI. A Tool Augmented Framework for Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Scenarios". I-Chun Chern, Steffi Chern, Shiqi Chen, Weizhe Yuan, Kehua Feng, Chunting Zhou, Junxian He, Graham Neubig, Pengfei Liu. Preprint: the only venue mark on the PDF is "arXiv:2307.13528v2 [cs.CL] 26 Jul 2023" (p1). 2023.

File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/chern-2023-factool.pdf

COVERAGE: 25 of 25 pages, 106,239 of 106,239 chars. Body p1-13, references p13-15 (skimmed for origins), Appendix A prompts p16-18, Appendix B example and error cases p19-25. Nothing skipped.

CLAIMS

- claim: FacTool is a five-step pipeline in which a deterministic tool, not the model's own recall, supplies the evidence.
  number: none
  setup: Claim extraction is always ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo). Query generation and verification use gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 or gpt-4-0314. Tools: Google Search via Serper (KB-QA), Python execution (code, math), Google Scholar via `scholarly` (citations).
  quote: "consists of five main components: claim extraction, query generation, tool querying, evidence collection, and agreement verification"
  where: p4

- claim: With GPT-4, FacTool beats the same model checking itself without tools on response-level F1 in all four tasks.
  number: 71.79 vs 57.14 (KB-QA), 92.11 vs 85.26 (code), 80.36 vs 70.59 (math), 94.74 vs 21.54 (scientific)
  setup: Baseline is Self-Check with 3-shot CoT, GPT-4. Responses all generated by ChatGPT. n responses (factual:non-factual) from Table 3: KB-QA FactPrompts 50 (23:27), HumanEval 164 (109:55), GSM-Hard 100 (47:53), scientific 100 (10:90). The positive class is "factual".
  quote: "71.79 v.s. 57.14 response-level F1 on KB-based QA, 92.11 v.s. 85.26 response-level F1 on code generation, 80.36 v.s. 70.59 response-level F1 on math problems, and 94.74 v.s. 21.54 response-level F1 on scientific literature review"
  where: p9, Table 5

- claim: The largest gain is on citation checking, where a lookup replaces model recall.
  number: claim-level F1 95.24 vs 36.71
  setup: GPT-4, 186 citation tuples (33 factual : 153 non-factual). Title and year are exact case-insensitive string matches; only the author-subset check uses an LLM.
  quote: "95.24 v.s. 36.71 claim-level F1 and 94.74 v.s. 21.54 response-level F1"
  where: p9

- claim: Self-check tends to pass false content as true.
  number: response-level precision 63.16 vs 87.50 (KB-QA), 76.43 vs 89.74 (code), 58.33 vs 69.23 (math), 12.73 vs 100.00 (scientific)
  setup: Self-Check (3) GPT-4 vs FacTool GPT-4, same sets as above.
  quote: "self-check models tend to classify claims as “True” considerably more frequently than FACTOOL, suggesting a lower sensitivity for error detection"
  where: p9-10 (line breaks removed from the quote)

- claim: Tools do not help when the verifier model is weak: with ChatGPT on KB-QA, zero-shot self-check beats FacTool.
  number: claim-level F1 84.88 vs 81.25; accuracy 75.54 vs 74.25
  setup: KB-QA FactPrompts, 233 claims (177:56), ChatGPT as verifier.
  quote: "reasoning errors are the main reason why FACTOOL powered by ChatGPT performs worse than the self-check baselines"
  where: p10; numbers from Table 5 rows "Self-Check (0) 75.54 90.40 80.00 84.88" and "FACTOOL 74.25 73.45 90.91 81.25", p9

- claim: Per-claim checks pass on math while the whole answer is still often wrong, because only arithmetic is checked, not reasoning.
  number: claim-level F1 98.97 vs response-level F1 80.36
  setup: GPT-4, GSM-Hard, 284 claims (246:38), 100 responses. Response labels come from the GSM-Hard target value.
  quote: "a 98.97 claim-level F1 / 80.36 response-level F1 on math problems"; "FACTOOL will not verify the reasoning process of the mathematical solution"
  where: p9; p11

- claim: LLM claim extraction is close to human atomic content units.
  number: ChatGPT ROUGE-1 F1 0.7836, BERTScore F1 0.7174; GPT-4 0.7860 and 0.7175
  setup: RoSE, 100 reference summaries, 527 claims. Average of the best match of each extracted claim to a gold ACU.
  quote: "ChatGPT ROUGE-1 0.7770 0.8285 0.7836"; "BERTScore 0.6958 0.7521 0.7174"
  where: p8, Table 4

- claim: Used as an evaluator, FacTool ranks GPT-4 the most factual chatbot.
  number: weighted claim-level accuracy 75.60, response-level 43.33; Vicuna-13B 50.35 and 21.67
  setup: 60 prompts (30 KB-QA, 10 code, 10 math, 10 scientific). FacTool (GPT-4) is treated as ground truth, with no human check.
  quote: "GPT-4 75.60 43.33 196.83"; "Vicuna-13B 50.35 21.67 207.13"
  where: p12, Table 6

LIMITS

Conceded by the authors:
- KB-QA failures: reasoning errors with sufficient evidence, conflicting evidence, ambiguous claims (p11).
- Code: generated tests lack variety, and majority-voted "pseudo-golden output" can be wrong when all generated solutions share a bug (p11).
- Math: round-off false negatives; no reasoning check (p11).
- Citations: title abbreviation and author matching failures; whether the cited paper is appropriate is "left for future investigation" (p4 footnote 2).
- Invalid JSON from the models forced reruns (p8 footnote 8).

Not shown:
- No confidence intervals or significance tests. Samples are small: 50 KB-QA responses, and only 10 factual scientific responses.
- Labels were annotated by "the authors collectively", with no inter-annotator agreement.
- All evaluated responses come from ChatGPT; the baseline is only the same model without tools.
- Claim extraction is scored only on RoSE summaries by surface similarity, not on the long-form responses actually verified. Missed or mangled claims are not measured.
- No cost, latency or number of calls.
- Evidence is short search snippets. Scholar check assumes the paper is the first hit.
- This is not RAG faithfulness: claims are checked against retrieved web evidence, never against a supplied context. It supports "claim by claim" decomposition, not groundedness to a given document.
- Dated: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, gpt-4-0314, Bard, Claude-v1, Vicuna-13B, ChatGPT plugins.

BUILDS ON
- RARR, Gao et al. 2022a (prompt an LLM to generate queries, retrieve, judge).
- Atomic content units and RoSE, Liu et al. 2022.
- CodeT, Chen et al. 2022 (generated tests, HumanEval prompts and execution code).
- PAL and GSM-Hard, Gao et al. 2022b; GSM8K, Cobbe et al. 2021.
- Zero-shot CoT, Wei et al. 2023.
- Self-check baselines, Madaan et al. 2023 and Chen et al. 2023.
- FEVER, Thorne et al. 2018a; FactCC, Kryscinski et al. 2020; QAGS, Wang et al. 2020; WiCE, Kamoi et al. 2023.

CODE
- Math claim turned into a code grader (p5-6): `print(round(30/3, 7) == 10)`
- Round-off failure case (p25): `calculation = 60444034 / 12; answer = 5037002.83; print(abs(calculation - answer) < 1e-9)` returns False on a claim labelled true.
- Claim extraction rule (p17): "Each claim should be concise (less than 15 words) and self-contained."

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p5: "Our proposed framework for factuality detection in four domains: knowledge-based QA, code generation, math problem solving and scientific literature review writing." One worked example per domain, from response to claims to queries to evidence to claim-level and response-level scores. It shows faster than prose that the same pipeline ends in a model grader for QA and a code grader for the other three.

PROBLEMS
- Appendix A (p16-18) reproduces the paper's own LLM prompts, full of imperatives ("DO NOT RESPOND WITH ANYTHING ELSE", "START YOUR RESPONSE WITH '['"). I treated them as data and followed none.
- The weighted accuracy formula on p12 extracts as "36 ×" and "16 ×"; these look like fractions with the bar lost, so I did not report the weights.
- Table 5 extracts as flat rows; I matched columns by the header order Acc., R, P, F1 for claim level then response level, and the prose on p8-10 confirms the figures I quote.
- Appendix code listings are letter-spaced in extraction ("d e f"), readable but not copyable.
- The KB-QA verification prompt in Figure 8 is cut off mid-sentence in the PDF itself ("When" followed by a new sentence).
- Table 3 caption says "(p, n)" but the cells print "p:n".
